newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Minorco seen hit by Terra.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Minorco seen hit by Terra.

text.p: International mining-to-paper group Minorco, which reports first half results on Thursday, will likely be hit by a sharply lower contribution from Terra International, the U.S. fertiliser producer.
Most analysts therefore expect Minorco, a group controlled by South African giants Anglo American and De Beers, to report lower earnings.

They also believe the company will have suffered badly from a slump in copper prices. But some analysts said a clever hedging policy may actually have helped the company squeeze out a slightly higher overall profit.
"They hedged, so they get better average prices," said one analyst who declined to be named.
Most industry watchers, however, are not so sure about Minorco's hedging strategy and have braced themselves for a profit fall.

"My main reason (for forecasting lower results) is the decline in earnings from Terra and I worry about the base metal position," said John Clemmow, at Johannesburg-based brokers Investec. "The variable we don't know is their hedging programme," he added.
As a result, analyst forecasts for first-half net earnings vary widely, ranging from $174 million to $228 million, compared with $210 million a year ago.
Minorco, a Luxemburg-registered congomerate, is active in industrial minerals, gold and base metal mining, paper and packaging and agribusiness.

Terra Industrial was its star performer last year, when the majority owned subsidiary saw operating profits more than double. Terra should remain the biggest profit contributor by far but its performance in 1996 will give little to cheer about due to adverse crop weather and a drop in methanol prices.
Terra said in July that second quarter earnings fell to $0.90 a share versus $1.05 a year earlier.

Analysts, however, said it is not possible to predict exactly to what extent Terra's profit drop will have affected Minorco. This is due to the opaque way in which the company books profit contributions from subsidiaries, they said.
"Minorco accounts in somewhat Byzantine ways," said one analyst.
All analyst forecasts exclude exceptional gains due to divestments such as the sale of Minorco's 9.9 percent stake in Johnson Matthey in June.
